findings.statement: Marketplace review has three stages: automated checks, a preliminary review of the listing and scopes, and a functional review where a reviewer installs and tests the app.
Preliminary review takes up to 10 business days for feedback; functional review takes up to 10 weeks for new submissions, or 6 weeks for an already-listed app resubmitting changes.
Apps need at least 10 active workspaces (used in the past 28 days) and 10 weekly active users before they're eligible to submit for Marketplace listing.
findings.sourceTitle: Distributing your app in the Slack Marketplace

findings.statement: You need a publicly accessible landing page with an install link and a linked privacy policy, plus a support page offering a direct contact method with about a 2-business-day response expectation.
findings.sourceTitle: Distributing your app in the Slack Marketplace

findings.statement: Your privacy policy must cover what data is collected, how long it's kept, how people can access or delete it, and a contact method - a physical address alone isn't considered sufficient.
findings.sourceTitle: Distributing your app in the Slack Marketplace
findings.excerpt: A physical address alone is not sufficient.

findings.statement: Slack may run an advanced security review at any point after submission; apps that fail it may be blocked or removed.
findings.sourceTitle: Distributing your app in the Slack Marketplace

findings.statement: Avoid requesting scopes for features you haven't built yet, and avoid legacy, broad-access, or coded-workflow scopes (such as admin.*, search:read, triggers:*) before you're ready to use them.
An admin scope like admin.apps:read requires the app to be installed by an Enterprise org admin or owner, and installed across the whole org rather than a single workspace.
findings.sourceTitle: OAuth 2.0 in Slack - Bot vs User Tokens
findings.excerpt: Admin or Owner of an Enterprise organization

findings.statement: Composio offers a managed Slack OAuth app by default, so you don't have to register your own; switching to your own custom Slack app changes the consent-screen branding, scopes, and rate limits.
Common rejection causes include submissions not ready for review, requesting scopes for unbuilt features, inability to install or test with the credentials provided, and leftover test slash commands.
The live, published version of an app is locked; any change to its configuration, features, or scopes requires resubmission and another round of review.
Migrating a classic app to granular permissions cannot be undone and forces every existing installing user to reinstall the app.

Adding new features or scopes to a published app generally requires a new demo video and a staging app for re-review; purely cosmetic changes (name, icon, description), pricing, supported languages, and endpoint URL updates typically don't.
Reviewers can only access accounts created specifically for testing with dummy data, not real Slack workspaces, so you must provide Slack a way to install and test the app themselves.
Distributing through the Marketplace means agreeing to the App Developer Policy, Slack Marketplace Agreement, Security Review terms, API Terms of Service, and Brand Guidelines.

findings.statement: Unlisted public distribution lets an app be installed on any number of workspaces via an OAuth flow without going through Slack Marketplace review; it's intended for pilots with early customers, while commercial distribution is recommended to go through Marketplace listing.
findings.excerpt: running a pilot for early customers

findings.statement: Unlike unlisted distributed apps, apps listed in the Slack Marketplace are reviewed against Slack's requirements and guidelines.
findings.excerpt: Unlike unlisted distributed apps, apps listed in the Slack Marketplace are reviewed

findings.statement: A workspace can turn on 'app approval' requiring admin review for all app installs, including unlisted ones; an app not listed in the App Directory also shows installers a warning that it hasn't been reviewed by Slack.
findings.sourceTitle: Manage app approval for your workspace

claim.text: Both the unlisted-distribution and Marketplace-listing paths are self-serve; no partner program or vetting step is mentioned.
Apps listed in the Slack Marketplace are reviewed against Slack's requirements and guidelines, unlike unlisted distributed apps.
Admin-level scopes require an Enterprise org admin or owner to install the app, and a workspace can separately require admin approval for every app install regardless of listing status.
Unlisted public distribution has no workspace cap - it's explicitly meant to scale from one workspace to potentially hundreds before any Marketplace review.

tierReason.text: Slack Marketplace listing goes through a reviewed, multi-stage process (unlike unlisted distribution), with a preliminary stage and a separate functional stage that can together take weeks.

claim.text: Preliminary review takes up to 10 business days, and functional review takes up to 10 weeks for a new submission (6 weeks for a resubmission of an already-listed app).

scopeForks.text: Using only Slack's unlisted public distribution instead of Marketplace listing, Tier 1 applies: no Slack review, and the app can be installed on any number of workspaces. Unlisted apps show installers a warning that they haven't been reviewed by Slack, and a workspace's own admin-approval setting can still block any install regardless of listing.

claim.text: Composio offers a managed Slack OAuth app by default, so a developer can skip registering their own Slack app entirely.

whatYouLose.text: On Composio's managed app, the consent screen shows Composio's name and branding instead of yours, and scopes/rate limits are shared and fixed rather than something you control.

whenToSwitch.text: Switch to your own custom Slack app once you need your own branding on the consent screen, different scopes, or your own rate limits.

flow.text: A developer builds an OAuth 2.0 install flow, activates unlisted public distribution to reach any workspace, and - if pursuing Marketplace listing - submits for a preliminary then a functional review.

appTypes.text: Unlisted apps are installed directly via a shareable URL or Add-to-Slack button; Marketplace-listed apps additionally appear in Slack's public App Directory.

tokenNotes.text: Bot tokens are limited to the single workspace that installed the app; app-level tokens are a separate credential used mainly for Socket Mode connections.

scopes.allows: Read or manage settings across an entire Slack Enterprise organization.
scopes.neededFor: Org-wide admin tooling rather than a single workspace integration.

claim.text: Admin scopes require installation by an Enterprise org admin or owner, across the whole org rather than one workspace.

scopes.scope: Coded-workflow and broad-access scopes (e.g. search:read, triggers:*)
scopes.allows: Broad read access across workspace data, or building automated workflows.

claim.text: Slack's Marketplace guide specifically warns against requesting legacy, broad-access, or coded-workflow scopes before you're ready to use them.

claim.text: Marketplace listing requires a landing page with an install path and privacy-policy link, and a support page with about a 2-business-day response expectation.

prerequisites.item: A privacy policy covering data collected, retention, deletion rights, and a real contact method

claim.text: The privacy policy must cover what's collected, how long it's kept, how people can access or delete their data, and a contact method beyond just a physical address.

steps.title: Found Slack's app distribution and Marketplace review docs
steps.detail: The research stage located Slack's unlisted-distribution guide and its Marketplace review guide.

claims.text: Slack documents both unlisted distribution and Marketplace listing at docs.slack.dev.

steps.title: Build your OAuth 2.0 install flow
steps.detail: Without it, the app only installs into its own development workspace.

claims.text: An OAuth 2.0 flow is required before the app can be installed to any workspace beyond its own.

steps.title: Activate unlisted public distribution
steps.detail: Complete the Manage Distribution checklist to get a shareable install URL - no Slack review needed for this step.

claims.text: Unlisted public distribution is a self-service activation step with no Slack review.

steps.title: Request only the scopes you need right now
steps.detail: Avoid legacy, broad-access, or coded-workflow scopes before you're ready to use them.

claims.text: Slack warns against requesting scopes for features you haven't built yet.

steps.title: Live on any workspace that installs your unlisted app
steps.detail: At this point the app works for real users with no Slack review - this is the whole integration for most non-commercial or pilot use.

steps.title: Build a public landing page and support page for Marketplace listing
steps.detail: Needed only if you want App Directory/Marketplace listing: an install path, privacy-policy link, and a support contact method.

claims.text: Marketplace listing requires a public landing page and a support page with a direct contact method.

steps.title: Write a privacy policy that meets Slack's requirements
steps.detail: Cover what's collected, retention, deletion rights, and a real contact method.

claims.text: Slack's privacy-policy requirements go beyond a bare physical address as a contact method.

steps.title: Draft your scope justification
steps.detail: Use the Scope justification helper to prepare reviewer-facing notes for each scope you request.

steps.title: Draft a reviewer test plan with dummy test accounts
steps.detail: Reviewers can only use accounts made specifically for testing, never a real workspace's data.

steps.title: Reach 10 active workspaces and 10 weekly active users, then submit for Marketplace review
steps.detail: This is a real-adoption threshold, not a one-time setup task.

claims.text: Marketplace submission requires at least 10 active workspaces and 10 weekly active users first.

steps.title: Respond to preliminary and functional review feedback
steps.detail: Each resubmission can reset your place in the preliminary-review queue.

claims.text: Review has a preliminary stage and a separate functional stage, each of which can return feedback requiring a resubmission.

steps.title: Approved and listed in the Slack Marketplace
steps.detail: Once review passes, the app appears in Slack's public App Directory.

provider.what: Runs a preliminary review of the listing and scopes, then a functional review that installs and tests the app; only required for Marketplace listing, not unlisted distribution.

claims.text: Marketplace listing goes through a preliminary review stage and a separate functional review stage.

customerAdmin.who: An Enterprise org admin/owner (for admin-scoped apps), or any workspace that has app-approval turned on
customerAdmin.what: Admin scopes need an org admin or owner to install; a workspace can also require admin approval for every app install, listed or not.

claims.text: Admin-level scopes require an Enterprise org admin or owner, and workspace-level app approval settings can gate any app's install.

endUser.who: The person installing the app in their workspace
endUser.what: Grants authorization through Slack's OAuth consent screen; unlisted apps additionally show a not-reviewed-by-Slack warning.

claims.text: Installers see Slack's standard OAuth consent screen, with an extra not-reviewed warning for unlisted apps.

stuckPoints.reason: Submission is returned as 'not ready for review'
stuckPoints.fix: Make sure the app is production-ready, fully installable end-to-end (including uninstall), and free of leftover test artifacts before resubmitting.

claim.text: Slack returns submissions it considers not ready for review, including ones with bugs or a poor user experience.

stuckPoints.reason: Rejected for requesting scopes you don't use yet, or broad/coded-workflow scopes
stuckPoints.fix: Remove any scope your current features don't actually use, and avoid legacy or coded-workflow scopes until you need them.

claim.text: Requesting scopes for unbuilt features, or legacy/broad-access/coded-workflow scopes, is a documented rejection reason.

whileYouWait.text: Unlisted public distribution lets you run a full pilot with early customers, on any number of workspaces, with no Slack review at all.

keepsComingBack.text: The published app is locked - any change to configuration, features, or scopes needs resubmission and another review pass, and Slack can also run an advanced security review at any point after approval.

hardToUndo.text: Migrating a classic app to granular permissions cannot be undone, and it forces every existing installing user to reinstall the app.
